# v2.75-dev — disable a user account instead of deleting it

Until now, the only way to stop someone signing in was to delete their account — which also threw away their login history, their role and their company access. Offboarding a leaver or suspending an account for a few weeks shouldn't be a one-way door.

## What's new

**You can now disable and re-enable a user account.** In **Admin → Users**, each row has a new power icon in the Actions column.

**Disabling takes effect immediately — including for someone already signed in.** They're signed out on their very next click, not whenever their session happens to expire. They then can't sign back in.

**Nothing is lost.** Their role, company access, MFA setup and login history are all kept, so enabling the account later restores it exactly as it was. When you disable someone you can record an optional reason ("Left the company", "On extended leave"); it's shown to other admins in the tooltip on the grey **Disabled** badge next to their role, along with who disabled the account and when. Disabled rows are greyed out so they're easy to pick out of the list.

**Guardrails.** You can't disable your own account, and you can't disable the last SuperAdmin — so nobody can accidentally lock everyone out of the admin pages.

**A disabled user gets the ordinary "Invalid username or password" message** when they try to sign in. That's deliberate: a distinct message would confirm to an attacker that the username is real. The attempt still shows up for you in the **Failed login attempts** panel with the reason *Account disabled*, so you can see when someone has tried.

## Also in this release

- The **last SuperAdmin** checks on *demote* and *delete* now ignore disabled SuperAdmins. Previously, if your only other SuperAdmin was disabled, the app would still let you demote or delete the last usable one — leaving nobody able to administer the system.
- In the Users table, the MFA column now reads **Off** rather than *Disabled*, so it can't be misread as referring to the account itself.
- Disabling or enabling an account no longer needs a page refresh to show, and a request for a user who doesn't exist now returns a clean "not found" rather than a server error.

## Upgrading

This release adds three columns to the users table. The update applies the migration for you; every existing account stays enabled.
